method_card.title: Tourist Attractions and Eating Out
method_card.content:
This lesson covers tourist attraction vocabulary, ordering in a restaurant and describing what you did using past tenses. It also practises partitive articles (du / de la / des) for ordering food and drink.

FrenchEnglish
un muséea museum
un monumenta monument
un châteaua castle / château
une cathédralea cathedral
une toura tower
le marchéthe market
visiterto visit
prendre des photosto take photos
je voudrais commanderI would like to order
l'entrée (f)the starter
le plat principalthe main course
le dessertthe dessert
l'addition (f)the bill
délicieux / délicieusedelicious
(Higher) le patrimoine(Higher) heritage / historic sites

Partitive articles for ordering: Use du (masculine noun), de la (feminine noun), de l' (before vowel), des (plural) for unspecified quantities. Example: Je voudrais du poulet et des frites, s'il vous plaît. After negation, partitives become simply de: Je ne mange pas de viande.

Talking about past visits: Use passé composé for what you did (j'ai visité, j'ai vu) and the imperfect for descriptions and opinions (c'était magnifique, il y avait beaucoup de touristes).

Model paragraph: Hier, j'ai visité le château et j'ai pris des photos. C'était impressionnant! Le soir, nous avons mangé dans un restaurant au centre-ville. J'ai commandé du poisson avec des légumes. Le repas était délicieux. (Yesterday, I visited the castle and took photos. It was impressive! In the evening, we ate in a restaurant in the town centre. I ordered fish with vegetables. The meal was delicious.)
steps: Learn the key tourist attraction and restaurant vocabulary
Master partitive articles (du / de la / des) for ordering food and drink
Use the passé composé for what you did and the imperfect for descriptions
Build extended sentences combining sightseeing and eating-out contexts

exam_context.frequency: Restaurant role-plays and tourist-visit writing tasks are highly frequent

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'J'ai visité le château et j'ai pris des photos. C'était magnifique!'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Identify the tenses: j'ai visité and j'ai pris = passé composé. C'était = imperfect (description/opinion).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: j'ai visité le château = I visited the castle. j'ai pris des photos = I took photos (pris = irregular past participle of prendre).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: C'était magnifique = It was magnificent (imperfect for a past description).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I visited the castle and took photos. It was magnificent!

worked_examples.question: How do you choose between du, de la, de l' and des when ordering food?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Check the gender and number of the food noun: masculine singular → du (du pain), feminine singular → de la (de la soupe).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Before a vowel or silent h → de l' (de l'eau, de l'agneau). Plural → des (des frites).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: After negation, all partitives become de (or d' before vowel): Je ne mange pas de viande. Not de la or des.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: du (m sg), de la (f sg), de l' (before vowel), des (pl). After negation → de / d'.

bronze.question: Match the French tourist attraction vocabulary to the English meaning
Match the French restaurant vocabulary to the English meaning
Complete the sentences with the correct partitive article

gaps.correct_explain: du is used before masculine singular nouns: le poulet → du poulet.

wrong.de la: de la is for feminine nouns. Poulet is masculine, so you need du.
wrong.des: des is for plural nouns. Poulet is singular, so you need du.

gaps.correct_explain: des is used before plural nouns: les frites → des frites.

wrong.du: du is for masculine singular nouns. Frites is plural, so you need des.
wrong.de la: de la is for feminine singular nouns. Frites is plural, so you need des.

gaps.correct_explain: de l' is used before singular nouns starting with a vowel: l'eau (feminine) → de l'eau.

wrong.du: du is for masculine nouns that start with a consonant. Eau starts with a vowel, so you need de l'.
wrong.de la: de la contracts to de l' before a vowel. Eau starts with a vowel, so use de l'.

bronze.question: Complete the sentences about a tourist visit

wrong.visite: visite is the present tense or noun. The past participle needs an accent: visité.
wrong.visitais: visitais is the imperfect. The context needs the passé composé: j'ai visité.

gaps.correct_explain: pris is the irregular past participle of prendre (to take).

wrong.prendu: prendu is not a word. Prendre has an irregular past participle: pris.
wrong.prend: prend is the present tense il/elle form. The past participle is pris.

gaps.correct_explain: impressionnant (impressive) or any positive opinion adjective works here.

wrong.bien: bien (good) can work but is less precise than a descriptive adjective. Try impressionnant or magnifique.

bronze.question: What does 'J'ai commandé du poisson avec des légumes. C'était délicieux' mean?
options: I ordered fish with vegetables. It was delicious.
I am ordering fish with vegetables. It is delicious.
I ordered soup with vegetables. It was delicious.
I would like fish with vegetables. It was delicious.

bronze.question: Which phrase correctly orders 'some water' in French?
options: Je voudrais de l'eau, s'il vous plaît
Je voudrais du eau, s'il vous plaît
Je voudrais des eaux, s'il vous plaît
Je voudrais la eau, s'il vous plaît

bronze.source_text: Nous avons visité un château magnifique et j'ai acheté des souvenirs au marché. C'était une journée fantastique.
model_answers: We visited a magnificent castle and I bought some souvenirs at the market. It was a fantastic day.

bronze.audio_text: J'ai visité un musée et c'était intéressant.

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
silver.english: Yesterday, she visited the cathedral and she took photos.

gaps.correct_explain: visité is the past participle of visiter. No agreement needed with avoir.

wrong.visitée: visitée would only agree if la cathédrale were a preceding direct object. After the verb, no agreement: visité.
wrong.visite: visite is the present tense. You need the past participle visité (with accent).

gaps.correct_explain: pris is the irregular past participle of prendre.

wrong.prendu: prendu is not a word. The irregular past participle of prendre is pris.
wrong.prend: prend is the present tense il/elle form. The past participle is pris.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Je voudrais du soupe et de la pain, s'il vous plaît.
silver.explanation: La soupe is feminine, so the partitive article must be de la, not du (which is for masculine nouns).
silver.translation: I would like some soup and some bread, please.

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: I visited the Eiffel Tower and I took lots of photos.

distractor_labels.vu: vu means 'seen' (past participle of voir) — visité (visited) is more natural for a tourist attraction

silver.source_text: Yesterday, we ate in a restaurant in the town centre. I ordered some fish and it was delicious.
model_answers: Hier, nous avons mangé dans un restaurant au centre-ville. J'ai commandé du poisson et c'était délicieux.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: Yesterday, we visited a magnificent château and I took lots of photos. In the evening, I ordered fish with vegetables in a restaurant. The meal was delicious and it was a wonderful day.
model_answers: Hier, nous avons visité un château magnifique et j'ai pris beaucoup de photos. Le soir, j'ai commandé du poisson avec des légumes dans un restaurant. Le repas était délicieux et c'était une journée merveilleuse.

Check: passé composé (avons visité, j'ai pris, j'ai commandé — all with avoir), partitive article (du poisson, des légumes), imperfect for descriptions (était, c'était), adjective position (magnifique after noun). Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in French
gold.english: I would like to order the fish with vegetables and a dessert, please.

distractor_labels.du: when ordering a specific dish from the menu you say le poisson (the fish — definite), not du poisson
distractor_labels.veux: veux is less polite — voudrais (conditional) is better style when ordering in a restaurant

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are on holiday in France and have dinner at a restaurant in the town centre. The waiter comes to take your order.

bullets.prompt: Greet the waiter and ask for a table for two people.
bullets.model_answer: Bonsoir! Avez-vous une table pour deux personnes, s'il vous plaît?
bullets.note: greeting + Avez-vous (polite question) + pour deux personnes + s'il vous plaît

bullets.prompt: Order a starter and a main course.
bullets.model_answer: Comme entrée, je voudrais de la soupe à l'oignon, et comme plat principal, je voudrais du poulet avec des frites.
bullets.note: comme entrée / comme plat principal + je voudrais + partitive article (de la, du, des)

bullets.prompt: Say what you visited today and give your opinion.
bullets.model_answer: Aujourd'hui, j'ai visité le château et j'ai pris des photos. C'était impressionnant!
bullets.note: passé composé (j'ai visité, j'ai pris) + imperfect opinion (c'était)

bullets.prompt: Ask for the bill and say you will come back next year.
bullets.model_answer: L'addition, s'il vous plaît. Nous allons revenir l'année prochaine.
bullets.note: l'addition + nous allons revenir (near future) + l'année prochaine
